clue.text: Facial growth is bound to be painful

parts.note: if you are bound to do something you must do it
to ache is to hurt or be sore

explanation.surface: A beard or moustache that is sure to hurt as it grows in.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is hair grown on the upper lip, a kind of facial hair.

clue.text: Taking poor view of one million coypu, no end wild

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: no end means the last letter of the word coypu is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dim view of a huge number of wild rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the U from COYPU to leave COYP; 'wild' rearranges I, M and COYP.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sighted people literally see poorly, and figuratively lack foresight.

clue.text: Spear to secure meat for the pot

definitions.text: Spear to secure meat for the pot

parts.words: Spear to secure meat for the pot
parts.note: a pointed rod pushed through chunks of meat to hold them for cooking, read as a hunting spear

explanation.surface: A hunter's spear used to catch meat for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a metal or wooden pin used to hold meat together while it cooks.

clue.text: Subtle character. Albert MPS

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Subtle character. Albert MPS (9)': 'Subtle character' defines ALCHEMIST (Jonson's play), but 'Albert MPS' builds nothing; the scan is covered by a sticker at this point and a search found no fuller text

clue.text: The Household- Cavalry could not restore his position

definitions.text: The Household- Cavalry could not restore his position

parts.words: The Household- Cavalry could not restore his position
parts.note: the royal horse soldiers recall all the king's horses and men in the nursery rhyme, who failed to put a fallen figure back on his wall

explanation.surface: A fallen official whom even the monarch's guards cannot reinstate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Household Cavalry are the British monarch's mounted guards: 'all the king's horses' in the rhyme of the egg who fell off a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the egg-shaped figure falls from a wall and the king's horses and men cannot reassemble him.

clue.text: Old gravestones made from Egyptian slate

indicators.note: the answer is made from these letters, built out of them in a fresh order

parts.note: E is a standard abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: Ancient headstones carved out of Egyptian slate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' tells you to rearrange SLATE into STELA, then add E (Egyptian) at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stelae are upright inscribed stone slabs used in the ancient world as grave markers.

clue.text: Trunk came apart noisily in this way

indicators.note: noisily means the word for came apart is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: tore means ripped or came apart, and it is said like a rocky hill, a tor
so means thus or in this way

explanation.surface: A tree trunk splits with a loud crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' works on 'came apart': TORE is said like TOR. Add SO (in this way) and the whole sounds like 'tore so'.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Sort of colour bar useful for pale-faces?

definitions.text: Sort of colour bar useful for pale-faces?

parts.words: Sort of colour bar useful for pale-faces?
parts.note: a colour bar here is a literal stick of colouring, the kind applied to the mouth by those whose faces look pale

explanation.surface: A racial colour bar that suits white people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour bar' suggests racial segregation, and 'pale-faces' suggests race, but the bar is a stick of make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick comes as a waxy stick of colour, adding colour to a pale complexion.

clue.text: The idea of the get-away car?

definitions.text: The idea of the get-away car?

parts.words: The idea of the get-away car?
parts.note: the getaway vehicle exists to help someone flee, so its whole philosophy is fleeing reality

explanation.surface: Asking what purpose a robbers' getaway vehicle serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is the habit of seeking distraction from unpleasant reality, a mental flight.

clue.text: Time to change ends has arrived in knock out

parts.note: in cricket, after each over the bowling switches to the other end of the pitch
come, as in 'has come', means has arrived

explanation.surface: A sports match pauses so the teams can swap ends during a knockout tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six balls, after which bowling switches to the other end. 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to defeat them, much as a knockout does.

clue.text: Amount of latitude king reposed in a subject

indicators.note: the king rests inside the subject, so one word lies within the other

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch lounging around, given a lot of freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latitude' looks like it means freedom, but it is the geographical sense: a tropic is a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are fixed lines of latitude on the globe.

clue.text: Hasn't she done well, producing such splendid birds?

definitions.text: Hasn't she done well, producing such splendid birds?

parts.words: Hasn't she done well, producing such splendid birds?
parts.note: plays on the proverb that fine plumage makes fine birds, read as praise for a hen with handsome chicks

explanation.surface: Praise for a mother hen who has raised handsome chicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' is also British slang for young women, dressed in smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine feathers means smart clothes, from the proverb that elegant dress makes elegant people.

clue.text: One's to appear before the French department

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds an S
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone is due to appear in front of an official department in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear' is a link. The Isère is a French department named after the river that runs through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isère is an administrative region of south-eastern France, around Grenoble.

clue.text: Wretched over losing head cover

parts.note: thin can mean poor or feeble, as in a thin excuse, so wretched
on top means above or over

explanation.surface: A miserable person feels worse after a hat blows off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thin on top means going bald, losing the hair that covers the head.

clue.text: Falsifies the marks? Nonsense

parts.note: to fiddle the books is to falsify them
ticks are marks made on a page

explanation.surface: A teacher accused of altering the grades dismisses the charge as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old exclamation meaning rubbish or that is absurd.

clue.text: The last of Private Ortheris, perhaps, as a man of ideas

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged some other way
take only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The final word on one of Kipling's soldiers, Private Ortheris, as a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last of Private' gives E; 'perhaps' rearranges E with ORTHERIS. Private Ortheris is a soldier in Kipling's stories. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser forms theories, someone who deals in concepts and speculation.

clue.text: He sagged badly, these brainy people found

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are in poor order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man slumped, and these clever people discovered him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges HE SAGGED. 'these' and 'found' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is informal for intellectuals, people of high learning.

clue.text: Idling round the Square, being silly

indicators.note: round means the first word is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: fooling around is idling, wasting time
T, from the T-square, a drawing instrument shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Lounging about the town square, behaving foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Square' looks like a town square, but it is T, from T-square, placed inside FOOLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Footling means trivial or silly, wasting time on petty things.

clue.text: Even virtue is toned down here

parts.note: good, as a noun, means virtue
to temper something is to moderate or tone it down

explanation.surface: Even goodness is muted in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like part of the sentence, but it is the definition, as in even-tempered. 'here' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An even-tempered person is calm and not quick to anger.

clue.text: Innumerable people get called this

parts.note: in the Gospels a possessed man says his name is this word, 'for we are many', so a vast crowd bears the name

explanation.surface: A huge crowd being given a collective name.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a vast number, from the Roman army unit and the biblical 'my name is Legion'.

clue.text: Look up to the rider

definitions.meaning: Paul ..., the American patriot famed for his midnight ride of 1775

explanation.surface: Admire the horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to hold in deep respect; Paul Revere rode to warn of the British advance.

clue.text: South African mulled wine to knock back

parts.note: mulled wine is served heated, so hot
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: to knock something back is to send it back, so the word 'to' is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone in South Africa downs a glass of spiced wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like drinking, but it turns 'to' into OT. Tent is an old crossword word for a red Spanish wine. Hottentot is an old, now offensive, name for the Khoikhoi people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hottentot was a historic outsider's name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.

clue.text: Picked utensil up, holding piece of music

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
holding means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a kitchen tool while holding a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' marks letters inside 'Picked utensil' (EDUTE), and 'up' reverses them in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a short musical composition written as a technical study.

clue.text: "worthy Captain — , Commanding of The Mantelpiece" (Gilbert)

parts.note: fill the gap with the captain's name from W. S. Gilbert's Bab Ballads poem about the ship The Mantelpiece

explanation.surface: A line quoted from a comic poem by W. S. Gilbert, with the captain's name left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Captain Reece of The Mantelpiece is from Gilbert's Bab Ballads.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Reece is the kindly commander in Gilbert's comic poem of that title.

clue.text: Sounds of leave-taking — change is due

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters that follow

parts.note: as printed the words give five letters; the setter's fodder needs an A as well to make six

explanation.surface: Goodbyes being said because it's time for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, IS DUE gives only five letters; the setter must have meant an A in the fodder as well, perhaps 'a change'. Rearranged, those letters give the plural of the French farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: An adieu is a goodbye, so the plural is a set of farewells spoken on leaving.

clue.text: Exude through spike of flower

parts.note: per means by way of or through, as in per post
a spire is a tapering shoot or flower spike of a plant

explanation.surface: Something oozes out through the flower spike of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is to sweat, giving off moisture through the skin.

clue.text: The address for professional writers in Scotland

definitions.text: The address for professional writers in Scotland

parts.words: The address for professional writers in Scotland
parts.note: Scottish solicitors bear the title Writers to the ..., so the word after 'to' is where they are addressed

explanation.surface: Where Scottish authors might be sent their post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' are not authors: in Scotland the Writers to the Signet are a society of solicitors, and 'address' plays on 'to the', as on a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Signet is the Scottish royal seal, giving its name to the Writers to the Signet.

clue.text: Put off the English novel

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new or strange

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside an English novel unread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective meaning unfamiliar. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, making them turn away from you.
